summary.text: A nymph whom Apollodorus names as the mother of Bucolion, illegitimate eldest son of king Laomedon — the prose genealogy beside Homer's shepherd episode, where the only named fountain-nymph is Abarbarea, mother of Aesepus and Pedasus.

story.text: In Apollodorus' roll of Laomedon's children, the king begat Tithonus, Lampus, Clytius, Hicetaon, and Podarces, and the daughters Hesione, Cilla, and Astyoche, besides a son Bucolion by a nymph Calybe. No other ancient author in the atlas' seven lenses names her; Homer knows Bucolion as Laomedon's eldest, born of an unwed mother, and names a different fountain-nymph, Abarbarea, as the mother of Bucolion's twin sons.
